historical_record.description: The Park Branch Library, designed by the firm McDougall Brothers.
Photographed, showing the Park Branch Library.
The joint venture of Field Paoli and Joseph Chow & Associates presented its design for the branch's renovation to the Library Commission's peer review panel.
The new community rooms at the Park Branch Library were dedicated on August 4, 1983, with Mayor Feinstein attending.
Renovation and seismic strengthening of the Park Branch Library began on December 3, 1990.
With its renovation and seismic strengthening finished, the Park Branch Library was set to reopen on February 10, 1992.
The Art Commission approved a 44-by-26-foot mural design for the branch library on Page Street, submitted by Selma Brown and Ruby Newman, to be mounted on masonite panels.

The Art Commission approved alterations to the Park Branch Library: double metal doors from outside into a basement meeting room, the iron fence cut back at the sidewalk for a ramp down to the basement, and a new brick pier.

The Library Commission's branch committee reported that the Park Branch on Page Street near Cole was the only branch ever built with money from the Board of Supervisors, and had cost less than any other.
